text.text_excerpt: I grew up drinking coffee milk in Louisiana (Community, always) and progressed to regular coffee in high school (still only Community). Community Coffee is what all of my aunts, uncles, cousins, grandparents, parents, etc, kept in their pantries. Therefore I was happy to see a CC's so close to where I recently moved in. The Bananas Foster Latte is so good. This place is always clean and pretty big. It always seems to be filled with kids studying...which isn't a bad thing! :) There are a few tables outside but not many and these tend to always taken with people who have dogs. It's similar to other CC's I've been to before, but I'm a CC's fan. Sentimentalism + good location = winning.

I've always liked Community Coffee but this was my first time visiting a CC's. Here's a rundown of my first impressions: Local Flavor There's no mistaking you're in New Orleans the moment you step inside. Jazz music is playing softly overhead. Postcards of NOLA images (Mardi Gras Indians, beignets, streetcars, jazz musicians), coffee mugs and other merchandise are for sale. I've never seen that level of local celebration and support at any Starbucks and it's cool. Comfortable Atmosphere They've made it a pretty comfortable place to linger awhile. The décor is mellow and they have plenty of seating outside on the sidewalk and inside. Outlets are plentiful and it takes no time (and no code)...

I had a meeting at this CC's recently and it turned out to be the perfect place to grab a coffee and have a chat. The coffee is typical Community Coffee, so I'll spare you my thoughts on that. This review is for the space. This CC's is huge with plenty of tables and chairs and plenty of natural light flowing in through the windows that look out onto Magazine St. I love the whole "New Orleans" vibe of the place, right down to the New Orleans brass band music that was playing over the radio. There's a nice selection of sweet treats, if you're in the mood and the staff was really friendly and service was fast, even though there was a bit of a line.
